clue.text: Beastly assistant to the fish friar, say?

definitions.note: an adjective standing for a noun: the clue means 'a beast', the small striped rodent

indicators.note: the question mark and 'say' signal that the phrase is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a fish's assistant in a chip shop is the CHIP served alongside it, and a friar is a MONK

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about who helps the friar who fries fish.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'fish friar' is a pun on a fish fryer; his helper is a chip, and a friar is a monk. CHIP MONK said out loud gives the name of the striped North American squirrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The animal is a small ground squirrel, so it is a beast, which 'Beastly' points to loosely.

clue.text: See 24
Nick about to go mad, having been sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue 'sent up' means the run of letters is read from bottom to top, that is backwards

parts.note: re is Latin for 'about, concerning'
to flip is to lose one's temper or go mad

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick loses his mind after being mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been sent up' turns REFLIP round, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for to steal, a synonym for petty theft.

clue.text: Close to last time food warnings ensue

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

parts.note: hr is the abbreviation for hour, a unit of time
eats is informal for food

explanation.surface: Near the end of a meal, threats follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Threats and warnings are near synonyms: both announce trouble to come.

clue.text: A collection of equipment cuts up what the allies cut down

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the whole run of letters is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a kit is a set of equipment
saws means cuts, as with a saw

explanation.surface: A pack of tools cuts up something the Allies destroyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses A KIT SAWS as a whole, giving SWAS + TIKA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazi emblem was torn down by the Allied forces at the end of the Second World War.

clue.text: Not entirely 8 stand-up comedian in a month will be packing bags

indicators.note: one group of letters sits inside the month's name

parts.note: May is a month

indicators.note: not the entire word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: 8 across means sheepish, which here is read as sheep-like, ovine

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up reverses the letters

parts.note: a wag is a joker or comedian

explanation.surface: A stand-up comic is packing up for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle '8' (SHEEPISH) is used loosely to mean sheep-related, so it supplies a sheep adjective; 'stand-up' reverses the comedian and 'Not entirely' clips the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone packing bags is relocating, about to leave their home for somewhere new.

clue.text: Swimmer climbing mountain rocks

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means the word goes upwards, read backwards

parts.note: an alp is a high mountain
drinks on the rocks are served with ice

explanation.surface: A climber scales a mountain of rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaice is a flatfish, and any fish can be called a swimmer in crosswords.

clue.text: Endlessly utter expression of contempt, appearing embarrassed

indicators.note: without its end, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: utter and sheer both mean absolute
pish is an old exclamation of contempt

explanation.surface: Someone says something scornful and looks red-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheepish describes a person looking awkward or abashed after a mistake.

parts.note: read the cross-references as sheepish kangaroo: a kangaroo jumps, and a sheep's coat is fleecy

explanation.surface: A bare pair of cross-references to other answers.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is SHEEPISH and 20 is KANGAROO; a kangaroo is a jumper, and a sheep-like one would be fleecy.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted pullover made of wool, punned as a sheep-like animal that jumps.

clue.text: Difference when hot and cold reversed

indicators.note: the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a sink has hot and cold taps

explanation.surface: The difference made when the hot and cold supplies are switched.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a petty quarrel, and a difference can mean a disagreement.

clue.text: Individual, dead giveaway?

definitions.meaning: someone independent and unconventional, a true individual
cryptically, a ghost (spirit of the dead) that is given away for nothing

explanation.surface: A single person who reveals the truth too obviously.
explanation.definitionFit: An unconventional nonconformist is an individual; a gratis ghost is a dead giveaway.

clue.text: See 9
Power came with light switches when cool

parts.note: P is the symbol for power in physics

indicators.note: switching letters around rearranges them

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Power returned with the light switches when things cooled down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'came with light switches' reads as a power cut ending, but 'switches' is the anagram signal and 'with' only joins the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegmatic means calm and unemotional, so cool in temperament.

clue.text: In part of wedding cake, syrup beginning to get more sticky?

indicators.note: the following letters sit inside the cake layer

parts.note: wedding cakes are built in tiers
rhyming slang: syrup of figs means wig

indicators.note: the start of the next word, its first letter

explanation.surface: A slice of wedding cake with syrup gets stickier.
explanation.walkthrough: Syrup is Cockney rhyming slang (syrup of figs = wig). 'more sticky?' plays on twiggy meaning full of sticks, not gluey, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Twiggier means having more twigs, that is more sticks, punned as stickier.

clue.text: What comes up in cold climates is small, providing dressed as Scotsman?

definitions.text: What comes up in cold climates

indicators.note: being dressed in a garment puts the word inside the clothing

parts.note: a Scotsman's traditional dress is the kilt
providing means if, on condition that

explanation.surface: Something small that rises in snowy places, wearing a kilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed as Scotsman' stands for wearing a kilt, the Scottish national garment, so 'providing' sits inside it; the definition is a cryptic description of a lift that rises in snowy resorts.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski lift carries skiers up the mountain in snowy resorts.

clue.text: For containing single sign of danger, old safety measure

indicators.note: the first word holds the others inside it

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, means single
red is the colour that signals danger

explanation.surface: A single red warning sign as an old-fashioned safety precaution.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire door, slowing the spread of flames, is a safety measure in buildings.

clue.text: Support involving something 8 is a lifesaver

indicators.note: involving means wrapping around, so one piece takes in another

parts.note: a mast is an upright support
8 across read as sheepish: something sheep-like is a ewe

explanation.surface: A supporting structure involving something sheepish saves a life.
explanation.walkthrough: A Mae West was a WWII inflatable life jacket, named after the buxom film star.
explanation.definitionFit: This inflatable life jacket used by airmen saved lives at sea.

clue.text: Left in dark

definitions.meaning: the Latin and heraldic word for left
... also means menacing, dark and evil

explanation.definitionFit: The word means left in heraldry and evil or threatening in general use.

clue.text: Having grasped meaning initially, studies sentence

parts.note: to con is to study, to pore over

indicators.note: holding something tightly, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a den is a study, a private room

indicators.note: at the start, so the first letter

explanation.surface: After grasping the meaning, someone studies a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'studies' gives two words for study, CON and DEN, which grasp M from 'meaning initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: To condemn someone is to pass sentence on them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Boxer with no time for fancy steps smothering a right, punching conclusive blow

indicators.note: punching a hole in something puts letters inside it

parts.note: a KO, knockout, ends a fight

indicators.note: smothering means covering over, so these letters wrap around others
without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a tango is an elaborate dance

explanation.surface: A boxer who skips dance steps lands a right for a knockout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no time' removes T from TANGO; ANGO 'smothering' A R makes ANGARO, which is 'punching' into KO.
explanation.definitionFit: Kangaroos famously spar with their forelimbs, so the animal is a boxer.

clue.text: PM still available? Victoria was not

definitions.meaning: the morning has been spent, so the afternoon is left
Queen Victoria is famously quoted as saying 'We are not ...'

explanation.definitionFit: The queen is famously said not to have been entertained, and morning used implies afternoon remains.

clue.text: Above that, sleeping?

annotationWithheld.why: Above that, sleeping? — BE(YON)D: 'sleeping' means in bed, so it gives BED and also signals the container; one word doing two jobs

clue.text: Discuss where cattle market could be favouring these?

indicators.note: discussing something means talking about it out loud

parts.note: byres are cowsheds, where cattle are kept

explanation.surface: A debate about which cattle market favours whom.
explanation.walkthrough: BYRES is a Scottish and northern British word for cowsheds. A buyers' market is one where prices favour purchasers.
explanation.definitionFit: A buyers' market is one favourable to purchasers rather than sellers.

clue.text: Pop idol for gold-diggers?

parts.note: pop as father, idol as what is adored: a rich older man is adored by women after money

explanation.surface: A pop star admired by prospectors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop idol' suggests a singer, but pop means dad, and gold-diggers are people seeking a wealthy partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A wealthy older man who lavishes gifts on a younger partner is admired by fortune hunters.

clue.text: Threaded through trousers, a short 2

indicators.note: the letters run through the words, lying inside them

explanation.surface: Something laced through a pair of trousers, a short belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 2 down is BELT, which serves as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a cloth band worn round the waist, a kind of belt.

clue.text: Safety measure testable when crashing

indicators.note: a crash wrecks things, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A safety measure that can be tested in crash tests.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat belt in a car is a basic safety device.

clue.text: Speller missing out "L" given lowest mark — 8 thing

indicators.note: missing out means leaving out the named letter

parts.note: someone who casts spells, the wizard Merlin
the lowest score possible is zero, O

explanation.surface: A speller who omits L gets the lowest grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 is SHEEPISH, read here as sheep-related.
explanation.definitionFit: The merino is a breed of sheep, so a sheep-related thing.

clue.text: Girl's 8 things holding artist back

definitions.note: girl's here is short for girl is

indicators.note: back means the whole run of letters is read in reverse
holding means containing, so a piece goes inside

parts.note: a teg is a two-year-old sheep
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A girl's sheep-related items hold back an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle 8 (SHEEPISH) is read as sheep-related, so '8 things' gives two sheep words; 'back' reverses everything, giving TERAGRAM read backwards. A teg is a sheep in its second year.
explanation.definitionFit: Margaret is a common female first name, so a girl.
